name: Egyptian
description: Ancient Egyptian star figures after Belmonte's map of the firmament, including the Bull's Foreleg (Big Dipper), Sah (Orion) and Sopdet (Sirius).
source: Stellarium sky cultures (github.com/Stellarium/stellarium-skycultures) - egyptian/index.json and description.md (contributed by Karrie Berglund, Digitalis Education Solutions, from J. A. Belmonte "A Map of the Ancient Egyptian Firmament"; reworked by Susanne M. Hoffmann)
Hoffmann, S.M., Hipparchs Himmelsglobus, Springer 2017 (cited by Stellarium)
Stars not in constellations.json taken from HYG v4.1 (github.com/astronexus/HYG-Database)
license: GPL-2.0 (Stellarium egyptian sky culture, "GNU GPL v2.0"); HYG v4.1 data CC BY-SA 4.0. GPL-vs-CC-BY-SA compatibility of the combined work has not been legally reviewed. Omission: the Egyptian decans are not defined in Stellarium and have no star list at hand from a credible open source, so they are skipped.

figures.name: Sopdet (Sirius)
figures.group: Belmonte map of the Egyptian firmament
figures.story: Sopdet (Greek Sothis) is the Egyptian name of Sirius, whose heliacal rising marked the start of the year and was linked to the goddess Isis. Marked as a single star (HIP 32349, named in the Stellarium Egyptian sky culture).
